one_line: Chief queen of Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana and an eminent Jain patron famed for her grace in music and dance.

appearance.age_look: Mid-20s, slender yet dignified, poised with a dancer’s lightness and a queen’s composure.
appearance.face: Heart-shaped face, warm medium-brown complexion, large expressive almond eyes with soft kajal, straight brows, slightly aquiline nose, small full lips; default expression serene and attentive, hint of a gentle smile.
appearance.hair: Long black hair parted in the middle and drawn back into a smooth, low bun at the nape; a narrow gold maang-tikka at the parting; delicate gold jhumka earrings; no crown, only a simple gold headband hugging the bun.
appearance.costume: Early 12th-century Hoysala court attire: a full-length silk sari in deep maroon with thin gold borders, draped in a South Indian style tightly around the waist and falling in modest pleats to the ankles; pallu drawn from back to front and neatly brought over the left shoulder, then across the torso to subtly cover the upper body; short-sleeved fitted blouse in muted leaf-green silk; a broad gold waist belt (oddiyanam) with floral motifs at the front; layered but not overly heavy gold necklaces (one short, one mid-length), slender gold bangles stacked on both wrists, and a simple toe ring visible on sandaled feet; fabric is smooth with minimal pattern, only fine gold edging and tiny stylised leaf motifs along the lower border.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript held gently in her right hand, one end slightly unfurling, symbolising her inscriptions and learned patronage.

ref_desc: Shantala Devi is a mid-20s, medium-brown, serene queen with long black hair in a low bun, maroon and gold South Indian silk sari, green blouse, gold jewellery, and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript, set in deep maroon, leaf green, warm gold and black tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Shantala Devi: a mid-20s Hoysala queen with a heart-shaped medium-brown face, large calm almond eyes lined with soft kajal, straight brows, slightly aquiline nose and gentle smile. Her long black hair is center-parted and pulled into a smooth low bun at the nape, accented by a narrow gold maang-tikka at the parting, simple gold jhumka earrings, and a thin gold headband wrapped around the bun. She wears an early 12th-century South Indian court sari of deep maroon silk with fine gold borders, draped modestly and tightly around her waist in neat pleats to the ankles, paired with a short-sleeved fitted blouse of muted leaf-green silk; the pallu comes from the back over her left shoulder and then across the torso, covering her upper body in a dignified manner. A broad gold waist belt with floral motifs sits at the front, with layered but light gold necklaces (one short, one mid-length) and slender gold bangles on both wrists; simple sandals and a glimpse of a toe ring complete the look. In her right hand she carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript, one end slightly unfurled, held with gentle confidence as her signature prop. Emphasise the fixed colours—deep maroon sari, leaf-green blouse, warm gold ornaments, black hair—and show her from front, three-quarter, and back views to capture face, hair, garments, jewellery, sandals and the palm-leaf manuscript clearly in a clean, neutral background.
